text: everybody what does it mean for all scripture to be failed navistos this is traditionally translated as God breathed and right off the bat I have to point
out that second Timothy was not written by Paul it was most likely written at the end of the first century or maybe the beginning of the second century but
uh I want to share some scholarship that was published last year the book is called the invention of the inspired text philological windows on the
theophonephita of scripture by John C Poirier and in this book Poirier reviews the earliest known occurrences of this
word theopenestos in text like The Testament of Abraham and The Sibling oracles and fragments from porphyry and pseudo-facilities and a number of other
texts and what he argues and I think quite persuasively is that the contexts for all of this usage all the way up
until the third Century CE and specifically origin of Alexandria the contexts indicate that this word does
not mean God breathed in the sense of inspired but means life-giving in the sense of God breathed the breath of life into
humanity and so II Timothy 3 16 according to this reconstruction of the earliest sense of the word would be all
scripture is life-giving and is useful for teaching for reproof for correction and for training in righteousness if you're
interested in this passage and in the development of the concept of inspired scripture I think this would be a great book to pick up
